name: Benzofuranylpropylaminopentane
summary: (–)-Benzofuranylpropylaminopentane (BPAP; developmental code name FPFS-1169) is an experimental drug related to selegiline which acts as a monoaminergic activity enhancer (MAE). It is orally active in animals.

pharmacology.text: At much higher concentrations, BPAP is also a monoamine reuptake inhibitor, specifically of dopamine and norepinephrine and to a much lesser extent of serotonin.

uses.text: BPAP has been studied in preclinical research for potential treatment of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, depression, and aging. It has been found to be active in multiple animal models of antidepressant action. It also attenuates reinstatement of methamphetamine-seeking behavior in rodents. The drug has been proposed for potential clinical development for use in humans.

fact.en: It came out of research on selegiline by the Hungarian chemist Joseph Knoll, who proposed a class he called activity enhancers: drugs that make nerve cells release more transmitter when they fire, rather than blocking reuptake.
fact.zh: 它源自匈牙利化學家 Joseph Knoll 對 selegiline 的研究。他提出一類他稱為「活性增強劑」的藥物：讓神經細胞在放電時釋出更多傳訊物質，而非阻斷回收。
fact.zhHans: 它源自匈牙利化学家 Joseph Knoll 对 selegiline 的研究。他提出一类他称为「活性增强剂」的药物：让神经细胞在放电时发布更多传讯物质，而非阻断回收。
